newsitem.title: USA: US layoffs up 19.7 pct in Feb vs Feb '96 -- report.
newsitem.headline: US layoffs up 19.7 pct in Feb vs Feb '96 -- report.

text.p: U.S. layoffs totaled 40,480 in February, up 19.7 percent from the 33,830 job cuts announced in February 1996, according to a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas Inc.
Layoffs declined 7.1 percent from the January 1997 total of 43,595, the report said.
The relatively high number of layoffs last month suggests companies are shedding jobs in an effort to control inflationary pressures, it said.
As it did in January, the retail sector led other industries in job cuts last month, according to the report.

"Overall, the economy continues to be strong with exceptional growth in many (geographic) areas, especially the southwestern and Pacific states," John Challenger, executive vice president of the outplacement firm, said in a statement.

"Increasing reports of labor shortages ... coupled with the high number of job-cut announcements leads me to believe that companies are utilizing job cuts to keep costs and prices down," Challenger said.
